task_instance: For a user invoking the skill to stand up enterprise RBAC, design and actually create a least-privilege OCI compartment hierarchy (shared-infra, security, dev/staging/prod each with compute/data children), attach dev-team and prod-team IAM policies at the correct level, create a 'dev-instances' dynamic group for Instance Principal auth, and add a tag-namespace for environment-based access control in the user's Oracle Cloud tenancy.
blocker_detail: The skill's stated deliverable (Output section) is real OCI resources: a created compartment hierarchy, IAM policies attached at the correct compartment level, dynamic groups enabling Instance Principal auth, and a tag namespace. Every step executes the OCI Python SDK IdentityClient (create_compartment, create_policy, create_dynamic_group, create_tag_namespace) or the oci CLI against a live tenancy, and the Prerequisites require the OCI Python SDK, a populated OCI config with valid user/fingerprint/tenancy/key credentials, and tenancy-administrator access to the root compartment. The office-assistant runtime cannot run code or the SDK/CLI at all, and the task inherently requires live cloud administrator credentials and a real Oracle Cloud tenancy to create and verify the resources. The safety rules also forbid pointing a run at any live account or tenancy. A text-only design of the hierarchy and policy statements can be written but is not the verified deliverable the skill produces (created, inspectable cloud resources), so the core intent cannot be achieved and verified in this runtime. No bundled script was missing; the code is inline in SKILL.md, so the blocker is the missing credentials/account and the inability to make the real API calls, not a missing skill file.
evidence: Read SKILL.md at the given path. Prerequisites demand: OCI Python SDK (pip install oci), OCI config at ~/.oci/config with valid credentials, tenancy-administrator access, Python 3.8+. Steps 1-5 each call oci.identity.IdentityClient methods (create_compartment, create_policy, create_dynamic_group, create_tag/create_tag_namespace) and Step 4 uses InstancePrincipalsSecurityTokenSigner; the Examples section runs an oci CLI dynamic-group list. All require executing code and authenticating to a live Oracle Cloud tenancy. This runtime cannot execute code or shell commands, has no OCI credentials, no OCI account/tenancy, and safety rules forbid targeting a live account. Therefore the actual deliverable (created compartments/policies/dynamic groups confirmed via list_compartments / CLI audit) cannot be produced or verified. Only result.json was written to the work directory.
